items.context: The plan includes a new POST /backlog/validate-globs API endpoint for path-existence checking. This requires Go backend work (new handler, doublestar dependency, tests). The UI feature (modal + client-side validation) is independently useful without it. Should we phase the API work or ship it all together?

options.label: Ship UI first (Phase 1+3+4), add API validation later
options.rationale: Unblocks the core UX immediately. Client-side syntax validation covers the most common errors. Path checking is a nice-to-have enhancement. Recommended because it delivers user value faster and reduces the initial scope.

options.label: Ship all phases together
options.rationale: Complete feature in one go. Users get full validation from day one. Larger scope but no follow-up needed.

items.topic: Testing approach: vitest component tests or Playwright E2E?
items.context: The plan lists component tests for AcceptanceGlobDialog and integration tests for BacklogDetailsPage. The existing codebase has both vitest component tests (e.g., backlog-card.test.tsx, plan-panel.test.tsx) and Playwright E2E tests. Component tests are faster and more focused; E2E tests catch real browser interactions but are slower. The locked-state and PATCH integration are best validated with component-level mocks.

options.label: Vitest component tests only
options.rationale: Matches existing test patterns in the codebase. Fast, focused, mock the API layer. Covers all acceptance criteria without browser overhead. Recommended because the feature is a UI component with well-defined inputs/outputs.

options.label: Vitest component tests + one Playwright E2E smoke test
options.rationale: Component tests for logic, plus one E2E test that opens the modal, types patterns, and saves. Catches real rendering issues but adds maintenance burden.

items.topic: Empty state UX: what to show when no patterns are set
items.context: Currently, when acceptance_allow or acceptance_deny is empty, the detail page shows nothing for that section. The modal needs to handle opening with empty arrays gracefully. Should we also add a visual prompt on the detail page to encourage setting patterns?

options.label: Empty textarea in modal, no detail page change
options.rationale: Simplest approach. Modal opens with empty textarea, user types patterns. Detail page stays as-is (no chips shown when empty). Recommended — keeps scope minimal and the edit button already signals editability.

options.label: Add 'No patterns set — click to add' placeholder on detail page
options.rationale: More discoverable — users see an explicit prompt. But adds detail page layout changes beyond the edit button.

items.topic: Textarea placeholder text and helper copy
items.context: Each textarea in the modal needs placeholder/helper text to guide users on the expected format. This is especially important since glob syntax isn't universally known.

options.label: Placeholder in textarea + helper text below label
options.rationale: Textarea placeholder shows example: 'scenarios/my-app/ui/**\nsrc/components/*.tsx'. Helper text below the label: 'One glob pattern per line. Relative to project root.' Recommended — provides format guidance without overwhelming.

options.label: Placeholder only, no helper text
options.rationale: Cleaner modal. Users who don't know glob syntax can look it up. Less hand-holding.

options.label: Collapsible 'Glob syntax help' section in modal
options.rationale: Full reference with examples (**, *, {a,b}, etc.). Most informative but takes space and most users won't need it.

items.text: The CLI `backlog update` 405 error persists — attempted to auto-set acceptance_allow via CLI and got HTTP 405. The acceptance_allow globs are defined in the plan but could not be saved to spec.json via CLI. This does not block UI development since acceptance_allow is a plan-level constraint, not a runtime dependency.

Codebase exploration confirmed: BacklogFormDialog already has acceptance_allow/acceptance_deny as comma-separated inputs (lines 360-398 of backlog-form-dialog.tsx). The new AcceptanceGlobDialog will NOT modify BacklogFormDialog — both will coexist. The form dialog handles item creation (simpler patterns expected), while the new modal handles editing on the details page (where patterns may be longer/more complex).
